artiest/sly-stone.text:
Sly Stone, born Sylvester Stewart, was born in 1943 in Denton, Texas, and grew up in Vallejo in Northern California. He died in 2025. His parents were deeply religious and encouraged music. As a child he sang gospel with his brother Freddie and his sisters. At an early age he had mastered keyboards, guitar, bass and drums. In the mid-1960s he worked as a producer at Autumn Records and as a disc jockey at a soul station in San Francisco, where he also played The Beatles and The Rolling Stones.

In 1966 he merged his band with Freddie's to form Sly and the Family Stone, a group of Black and white members, men and women. They had hits with Dance to the Music and Everyday People in 1968, Thank You (Falettinme Be Mice Elf Agin) and I Want to Take You Higher in 1969, and Family Affair in 1971. Important albums are Stand! from 1969 and There's a Riot Goin' On from 1971. Sly Stone fused soul, rock, psychedelia and gospel into a new, rhythmic music that strongly shaped psychedelic soul and funk.

In the mid-1970s drug use and unpredictable behaviour put an end to the group. Stone then recorded a few solo albums that had little success, including High on You in 1975. He performed or collaborated with Parliament-Funkadelic, among others. In 1993 the group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and in 2017 he received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. His autobiography was published in 2023.
artiest/sly-stone.listen: Listen to Everyday People. Notice how simple the message and the melody are, and how the singing is passed between different voices.

artiest/small-faces.text:
The Small Faces were an English rock and pop band from London, formed in 1965. The group consisted of the singer and guitarist Steve Marriott, the bass player Ronnie Lane, the drummer Kenney Jones and the keyboard player Jimmy Winston, who was replaced by Ian McLagan in 1966. In the mid-1960s the band was one of the most respected and influential mod groups, with hits such as Whatcha Gonna Do About It in 1965 and Sha-La-La-La-Lee and All or Nothing in 1966.

From 1967 the group grew into one of the most successful psychedelic bands in the United Kingdom, with Itchycoo Park among others and the 1968 album Ogdens' Nut Gone Flake. In 1969 Marriott left to start Humble Pie. The others carried on as Faces, with Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood. After Itchycoo Park became a hit again in 1975, the original line-up briefly came together again, and in 1977 and 1978 Playmates and 78 in the Shade were released.

The group's sound is raw and energetic, a bridge between British rhythm and blues and psychedelia. Critics use the word freakbeat for it. The Small Faces are regarded as one of the first sources of inspiration for Britpop, and the music journalist Jon Savage called them the group that foreshadows the early Sex Pistols. In 2012 they were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame together with Faces. In the course they appear alongside The Who and The Kinks as a band of the mods.
artiest/small-faces.listen: Listen to All or Nothing and notice the raw, soulful voice of Steve Marriott and the powerful guitar and organ. Can you hear what a mod song that comes out of rhythm and blues sounds like?

artiest/smokey-robinson.text:
Smokey Robinson is an American singer, songwriter and producer from Detroit, where he was born in 1940. He got his nickname as a child from an uncle who took him to cowboy films. He grew up in the neighbourhood of Aretha Franklin and listened to doo-wop groups on the radio. In 1955 he started, with school friends, the vocal group that would later be called The Miracles. In 1957 the group auditioned for Berry Gordy. Robinson had a notebook with him containing a hundred songs he had written himself, and Gordy was impressed above all by that.

The Miracles became one of the first acts on Gordy's new label Motown. Shop Around became the label's first million-seller in late 1960. After that came, among others, You've Really Got a Hold on Me, The Tracks of My Tears, I Second That Emotion and The Tears of a Clown. Robinson was a singer, writer and producer all at once. He sang in a high, soft voice and wrote lyrics full of clever wordplay about love and heartbreak. He also wrote hits for other Motown artists: My Guy for Mary Wells, My Girl and The Way You Do The Things You Do for The Temptations, and Ain't That Peculiar for Marvin Gaye.

Robinson also became a vice president of Motown. In 1972 he left The Miracles and a year later he began a solo career, with albums such as A Quiet Storm (1975) and Being With You (1981). He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987. As a writer he helped shape the sound of Motown in the 1960s, before Holland-Dozier-Holland largely took over that role.
artiest/smokey-robinson.listen: Listen to My Girl by The Temptations, written by Smokey Robinson. Notice the short bass line and the guitar motif at the start, and how the song then grows fuller, layer by layer, with strings and horns.

artiest/smokey-robinson-en-the-miracles.text:
The Miracles were a vocal group from Detroit, founded in 1955 by a group of teenagers from the same high school. Smokey Robinson, Ronnie White and Pete Moore had been singing together since they were eleven. After the names The Five Chimes and The Matadors, and with the arrival of Bobby Rogers and Claudette Rogers, the group was called The Miracles from 1958. The guitarist Marv Tarplin completed the regular line-up. Berry Gordy was impressed by Robinson's voice and by his notebook full of songs he had written himself. On Robinson's advice Gordy founded his own label, Tamla, the basis of Motown, in 1959.

Shop Around became the first Motown single to sell a million copies in late 1960. After that came You've Really Got a Hold on Me (1962), Mickey's Monkey (1963) and, under the new name Smokey Robinson & The Miracles, the album Going to a Go-Go (1965) with The Tracks of My Tears and Ooo Baby Baby. In 1970 The Tears of a Clown, which Stevie Wonder had helped to write, became a number 1. Robinson left the group in 1972 for a solo career.

The Miracles were Motown's first group and the model for all the groups that followed. Unlike most Motown artists, they wrote their own songs, and also many hits for label-mates, such as My Guy for Mary Wells and My Girl for The Temptations. Robinson became a vice president of the company. Characteristic of the group are Robinson's tender, high lead vocal and the soft harmony singing around it.
artiest/smokey-robinson-en-the-miracles.listen: Listen to The Tracks of My Tears and notice the short guitar motif with which the song opens. Hear how Robinson sings high and soft, while the other Miracles support him with harmonies.

artiest/snap.text:
Snap! was a German dance project of the producers Michael Münzing and Luca Anzilotti. They had worked together since 1985, including with Sven Väth in the group Off. In 1989 they started Snap!. They used American-sounding pseudonyms, Benito Benites and John Virgo Garrett III, because they thought the public held prejudices about German music. For the vocals and the raps they brought in American artists, such as the rapper Turbo B, who was serving as a soldier in Germany, and the singer Penny Ford.

The Power became a worldwide hit in 1990, with a number 1 in England and the Netherlands. Ooops Up, Cult of Snap and Mary Had a Little Boy followed, and the debut album World Power. In 1991 the singer Thea Austin joined, who co-wrote Rhythm Is a Dancer. Turbo B did not want that song as a single, but it was released in 1992 anyway, and it became Snap!'s biggest hit, with a number 1 in Germany, England and the Netherlands, among other countries. The song used a sample from Automan by the American group Newcleus. Around the release of the album The Madman's Return (1992) Turbo B left. Snap! carried on without a rapper and made Welcome to Tomorrow (1994).

Snap! is an early example of Eurodance: European producers in the studio, American voices in front of the camera and the microphone, and a mix of house beats, synthesizers, a sung chorus and rap in the verses. The line-up changed constantly, but the sound remained the producers'. In this way the group could change its face without changing its sound.
artiest/snap.listen: Listen to Rhythm Is a Dancer and notice the division of roles: the singer sings the chorus, the rapper fills the verses. Hear how the synthesizers and the beat run on throughout, so that the song keeps working on the dance floor.

artiest/snelle.text:
Snelle is the artist name of Lars Bos, born in 1995 and raised in Gorssel, near Deventer. He began as a rapper and became a pop singer, with a series of number 1 hits in the Top 40 from 2019. According to him, his artist name refers to how quickly he gets drunk.

Bos studied at the Herman Brood Academie. In 2016 he released the EP De Vier and in 2018 the debut album Lieve jongens. The breakthrough came in 2019: Scars and Plankgas went platinum, and Reünie became his first number 1 in the Top 40. That song is about the bullying he experienced as a child because of his cleft lip. Smoorverliefd (2020) he made with the insurer Interpolis, as a warning against texting on a bike. It spent three weeks at number 1. In March 2020, at the start of the coronavirus crisis, he made 17 miljoen mensen with Davina Michelle, a new version of 15 miljoen mensen by Fluitsma & Van Tijn. At 1 minute 47 seconds it is the shortest number 1 hit in the Top 40. Blijven slapen (2021), with Maan, spent ten weeks at number 1 and won an Edison.

Snelle belongs to a generation that first built an audience of its own through social media and streaming, and only then ended up with radio and the record company. He stands in a line that began with Osdorp Posse and the Nederhop of the 1990s: music from America, but in their own language and about their own subjects. After Lars (2021) and Achtentwintig (2023), Binnenspiegel was released in 2026.
artiest/snelle.listen: Listen to Smoorverliefd (2020) first as an ordinary love song and then watch the video. Only at the end does it become clear what it is about: the video ends with an accident, because someone is texting on a bike.

artiest/snoop-doggy-dogg.text:
Snoop Dogg, born Calvin Broadus in 1971, comes from Long Beach, California. He broke through in 1992 via his collaboration with Dr. Dre, first on the single Deep Cover and then on the album The Chronic, with Nuthin' but a 'G' Thang. His debut album Doggystyle from 1993 was produced by Dr. Dre and entered at the top of the Billboard 200 in its first week. It yielded the hits What's My Name? and Gin and Juice. His second album, Tha Doggfather from 1996, also debuted at number one.

After leaving Death Row Records he signed with Master P's label No Limit and released Da Game Is to Be Sold, Not to Be Told and No Limit Top Dogg, among others. In 2004 he had his first number one on the Hot 100 with Drop It Like It's Hot, together with Pharrell. Later, as Snoop Lion, he recorded a reggae album, Reincarnated from 2013, and in 2018 the gospel album Bible of Love. In 2022 he bought Death Row Records and took part in the Super Bowl show.

Snoop is known for his laid-back, melodic rap style. He helped shape G-funk and the gangsta rap of the western United States, with heavy bass lines and soulful samples. He raps about drugs and violence in a relaxed tone. He is regarded as one of the greatest rappers of all time. In School of Rock, Nuthin' but a 'G' Thang and Still D.R.E. belong to the story of West Coast hip hop.
artiest/snoop-doggy-dogg.listen: Listen to Nuthin' but a 'G' Thang. Notice the laid-back, leaning-back way of rapping and the heavy bass line and the high synthesizer beneath it.

artiest/soft-cell.text:
Soft Cell was an English synth-pop duo of the singer Marc Almond and the instrumentalist David Ball. They met in 1977 at art college in Leeds and began making music together a year later. According to Ball they wanted to write catchy but twisted pop songs, in the spirit of Throbbing Gristle and Cabaret Voltaire, but more melodic. They paid for the first EP, Mutant Moments (1980), with a loan from Ball's mother. Their first single, Memorabilia, caught on in the clubs, but did not make the chart.

The record company gave them one last chance. The duo chose a cover of Tainted Love, an almost forgotten Northern soul song by Gloria Jones. In 1981 their version reached number 1 in seventeen countries, including England. The debut album Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret (1981) followed, with Bedsitter and the ballad Say Hello, Wave Goodbye. Then came Torch and What!, and the albums The Art of Falling Apart (1983) and This Last Night in Sodom (1984). Fame and drugs took their toll, and in 1984 the duo stopped. From 2001 they came back a few times. Ball died in 2025.

Soft Cell set a soul voice and a sense of drama against cool synthesizers. The lyrics were about nightlife, loneliness and the dark side of the city. Memorabilia is regarded as an early forerunner of techno, and artists such as Pet Shop Boys, Erasure and Nine Inch Nails named the duo as an influence. Tainted Love shows well how synth-pop in the 1980s gave older Black dance music a new, electronic look.
artiest/soft-cell.listen: Listen to Tainted Love and notice how little there is: an electronic rhythm, a few short synthesizer notes and Almond's vocals. Where a soul band played in the original, here two people with electronics do the work.

artiest/soft-machine.text:
Soft Machine is an English band from Canterbury, in Kent. Mike Ratledge, Robert Wyatt, Kevin Ayers, Daevid Allen and Larry Nowlin founded it in 1966. The name comes from the novel The Soft Machine by William S. Burroughs. Together with Pink Floyd the group played in the early years in the London underground clubs, such as the UFO Club. In 1967 the first single, Love Makes Sweet Music, was released. After a tour of France, Daevid Allen was not allowed back into the country and then started Gong. In 1968 the band supported the Jimi Hendrix Experience on two American tours.

The debut album The Soft Machine came out in 1968 and still sounded psychedelic. On Volume Two from 1969 the music moved towards progressive rock and jazz rock, and Third from 1970 and Fourth from 1971 completed that step. From 1971 Soft Machine made only instrumental music. The band had a long series of other members, among them Hugh Hopper, Elton Dean, John Marshall, Karl Jenkins, Roy Babbington and Allan Holdsworth. Albums such as Fifth, Six, Seven, Bundles and Softs followed until 1978, when the group stopped.

Soft Machine had little commercial success, but is regarded as one of the most important players of the Canterbury scene and as one of the first progressive rock bands. The AllMusic account calls it one of the most influential underground bands of its time. After a brief return in the 1980s, Soft Machine Legacy came into being in 2004. Since 2015 that group has played again under the old name, with the albums Hidden Details, Other Doors and Thirteen, among others.
artiest/soft-machine.listen: Listen to a track from Third from 1970. Notice how long the pieces run, how jazzy the improvisations sound and how Ratledge's electric organ colours the sound.

artiest/sol-ho-opi-i.text:
Sol Hoʻopiʻi, born Solomon Hoʻopiʻi Kaʻaiʻai, was a Hawaiian lap steel guitarist, born in Honolulu in 1902 as the twenty-first child in a large family. His family taught him to sing and play. At three he played the ukulele, and as a teenager he chose the Hawaiian steel guitar. At seventeen he is said to have sailed on a steamship with two friends, after which the passengers, charmed by their playing, collected the money for the crossing. In San Francisco and later Los Angeles he played in clubs. In 1924 he formed the Sol Hoʻopiʻi Trio in Los Angeles, which performed in the Polynesian-style nightspots that were popular at the time.

He made his best-known recordings between 1933 and 1938 with his Novelty Trio, Quartette and Five, for Decca and Brunswick, with songs such as Hula Girl and Ten Tiny Toes. He first played acoustic, but around 1935 switched to electric lap steel and developed a tuning of his own alongside the usual open A or open G. He often gave the standards of Tin Pan Alley, but also classic Hawaiian songs, a bluesy or jazzy treatment. In 1938 he gave up his worldly existence to play for the evangelist Aimee Semple McPherson. In his last years he went blind, but he kept playing, composing and teaching. He died in 1953.

His idiosyncratic rhythm, harmony and melody influenced not only Hawaiian musicians, but also steel guitarists from country and Western swing, such as Joaquin Murphy and Jerry Byrd. In 2012 the Library of Congress added his recording of Fascinating Rhythm to the National Recording Registry.
artiest/sol-ho-opi-i.listen: Listen to Hula Blues and notice the gliding sound of the steel guitar, which moves through the music like a singing voice. Can you hear how there is jazz and blues in the Hawaiian playing?

artiest/solomon-burke.text:
Solomon Burke, born James Solomon McDonald in 1940, was an American singer who became one of the founders of soul in the 1960s. He died in 2010. He was known as King Solomon and as the King of Rock 'n' Soul. His best-known records date from the first half of the 1960s, with hits such as Cry to Me, If You Need Me, Got to Get You Off My Mind, Down in the Valley and Everybody Needs Somebody to Love.

Burke came from gospel, and he mixed it with jazz, country and blues. A singing style with supple, powerful delivery and a mixture of sacred and worldly themes gave early soul a face. In fifty-five years he released thirty-eight studio albums on at least seventeen labels. His album Don't Give Up on Me won a Grammy in 2003. In 2001 he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Jerry Wexler of Atlantic called him the best male soul singer. Because he had fewer hits than James Brown, Wilson Pickett and Otis Redding, he has been described as the most underrated singer of the golden age of soul.

In the course Burke appears under Nederpop: in 2010 a Dutch band recorded an album with the American soul singer. That shows how far his influence reached, well beyond his own country and time.
artiest/solomon-burke.listen: Listen to Cry to Me and notice how Burke begins the song, almost speaking, and then breaks out with his great voice. Can you hear the sermon from church coming back?

artiest/solomon-linda.text: Solomon Linda came from Pomeroy in Natal and sang in Johannesburg with his group the Evening Birds. In 1939 he improvised the song Mbube in Eric Gallo's studio, with a high falsetto melody, and soon afterwards sold the rights for ten shillings. The song later became Wimoweh by The Weavers and The Lion Sleeps Tonight by The Tokens. Only in 2006 did his family receive a settlement.
artiest/solomon-linda.listen: Listen to the original of Mbube and then to Wimoweh by The Weavers: the falsetto melody that Linda improvised at the end later became the chorus of a worldwide hit.

artiest/solomon-linda-s-original-evening.text:
Solomon Linda was a South African singer and composer, born in 1909 near Pomeroy in Natal. He grew up with traditional songs and at a mission school also came to know Western hymns and choir competitions. In 1931, like many young African men, he went to Johannesburg to look for work, and sang there in a choir, the Evening Birds. Later he started a new group under that name, with friends from Pomeroy: Gilbert Madondo, Boy Sibiya, Gideon Mkhize, Samuel Mlangeni and Owen Sikhakhane. They performed at weddings and choir competitions, in striped suits, bowler hats and two-tone shoes.

In 1939 Linda worked at the record company Gallo in Roodepoort. There, during a recording, he improvised the song Mbube. It became a great success, reportedly with more than a hundred thousand copies sold in nine years. Linda earned nothing from it: he sold his rights to Eric Gallo for ten shillings shortly after the recording. The group broke up in 1948. Linda died in 1962, at the age of fifty-three, and his family could not afford a headstone.

His music became a model for isicathamiya, the South African choral genre. He used more basses per part, a falsetto head voice in the men's singing and an urban flair, while the bass still preserved traditional choral sounds. Pete Seeger heard Mbube and recorded it with the Weavers in 1951 as Wimoweh. In 1961 it became The Lion Sleeps Tonight by The Tokens, a number one in the United States. It was later used in The Lion King. Only in 2000 did an essay by Rian Malan in Rolling Stone bring Linda's story to light.
artiest/solomon-linda-s-original-evening.listen: Listen to Mbube and notice the deep basses and the high, floating solo voice above them. Hear how the choir voices form a solid rhythm beneath which the leader improvises his line.

artiest/son-house.text:
Son House, in full Edward James House Jr., was an American Delta blues singer and guitarist, born in 1902. He was known for his highly emotional singing and his slide guitar. For years he was a preacher and opposed to worldly music. At twenty-five he switched to the blues. He brought with him the rhythmic drive, the powerful delivery and the intensity of his sermons and developed a style of his own from them.

Charley Patton, the most important blues musician of the Mississippi Delta, invited him to perform together and in 1930 took him along to a recording session for Paramount Records. The records came out at the start of the Great Depression, did not sell and did not lead to national fame. In the area he did remain popular, and together with Willie Brown he was the most important musician of Coahoma County in Mississippi in the 1930s. There he was a formative influence on Robert Johnson and Muddy Waters. In 1941 and 1942 Alan Lomax and John W. Work recorded him for the Library of Congress. The year after, he left for Rochester in New York State and gave up music.

In 1964 he was rediscovered, among others by Alan Wilson of Canned Heat. The album Father of Folk Blues was released in 1965. He relearned his repertoire and performed for young, mostly white listeners at folk festivals and in coffee houses. In the course his name appears in that connection, alongside Robert Johnson: the recordings in which young collectors searched for the real blues.
artiest/son-house.listen: Listen to Preachin' the Blues and notice the sharp slide guitar and the shouting, sermon-like singing. Can you hear how the rhythm of the guitar drives the voice forward?

artiest/sonny-clark.text:
Sonny Clark was an American jazz pianist and composer who played mainly hard bop. He was born in 1931 in Herminie, a small mining town in Pennsylvania, and moved to Pittsburgh at twelve. At twenty he stayed on in California, where he began playing with the saxophonist Wardell Gray. After that he worked with the clarinettist Buddy DeFranco, among others, with whom he toured the United States and Europe, and in 1956 with Howard Rumsey's Lighthouse All-Stars. In 1957 he accompanied the singer Dinah Washington and so moved to New York.

In New York Clark became a sought-after accompanist, partly because of his rhythmic way of comping. He recorded often for Blue Note, where he played with musicians such as Kenny Burrell, Donald Byrd, John Coltrane, Dexter Gordon, Art Farmer, Grant Green, Jackie McLean and Hank Mobley. He also contributed to sessions by Charles Mingus, Sonny Rollins and Billie Holiday. Under his own name he made albums such as Dial S for Sonny in 1957, Sonny's Crib and Cool Struttin in 1958 and Leapin and Lopin in 1961. Part of his work was released only after his death, such as Blues in the Night and My Conception in 1979.

Clark died in 1963, at the age of thirty-one, in New York. The official cause was a heart attack, but it was probably a heroin overdose. His friend Bill Evans dedicated the piece NYC's No Lark to him, an anagram of his name. In the 1980s and 1990s John Zorn recorded albums with Clark's compositions, including News for Lulu.
artiest/sonny-clark.listen: Listen to the title track of Cool Struttin. Notice how Clark's right hand lets the melody flow relaxed and bluesy, while the bass and drums lay down a calm, walking pulse.

artiest/sonny-greer.text:
Sonny Greer was an American jazz drummer and singer, best known for his work with Duke Ellington. He was born in 1902 in Long Branch, New Jersey, and grew up in Asbury Park. He taught himself to drum and sing, with only the help of a vaudeville drummer who gave him a few lessons. As a teenager he played with orchestras in seaside hotels on the New Jersey coast, and then for three years at the Howard Theatre in Washington. There he met Duke Ellington.

Greer was Ellington's first drummer. He played in his quintet, the Washingtonians, and went with him to the Cotton Club. When Ellington's orchestra became famous in the 1930s and 1940s, he was there throughout. Greer designed drums for the company Leedy and built an enormous set-up including bells, a gong, timpani and vibraphone. It stood on a platform and drew the eye of the audience. The trombonist Lawrence Brown said that Greer was almost as popular as Ellington, and Ellington's son Mercer related that Ellington gladly took advice from him.

His drinking became a problem from the late 1940s. In 1950, on a tour of Scandinavia, Ellington took a second drummer along, and in 1951 he dismissed Greer. After that Greer played in the group of Johnny Hodges, a former colleague from the orchestra, and with Red Allen and Tyree Glenn, among others. In 1958 he appeared in Art Kane's famous photograph A Great Day in Harlem. He died in 1982.
artiest/sonny-greer.listen: Listen to a recording of Duke Ellington's orchestra from the 1930s. Try to hear Greer's drums, bells and gong beneath the ensemble, adding colour to the sound of the band.

artiest/sonny-rollins.text: Tenor saxophonist Sonny Rollins grew up in Harlem, where Coleman Hawkins lived nearby; Hawkins and Charlie Parker were his models. As a teenager he already played with Thelonious Monk and Bud Powell. In 1956 he recorded Saxophone Colossus, with St. Thomas, a calypso that refers to his Caribbean family. Rollins is known for thematic improvisation: in his solo he develops a small motif from the theme. On Way Out West (1957) he played without piano, with only bass and drums. In 1959 he withdrew from the scene and practised at night on the Williamsburg Bridge. In 1967 he played in the Netherlands with Han Bennink. He died in 2026, aged 95.
artiest/sonny-rollins.listen: Follow one motif from the theme: how often does it return in the solo, each time different?

artiest/sons-of-kemet.text:
Sons of Kemet was a British jazz band, formed by Shabaka Hutchings, Oren Marshall, Seb Rochford and Tom Skinner. After the first album Theon Cross took over the tuba from Marshall, and after the third album Eddie Hick joined on drums in place of Rochford. The line-up was unusual: saxophone and clarinet from Hutchings, a tuba instead of a bass, and two drummers. The group played a mixture of jazz, rock, Caribbean folk music and African music.

The debut album Burn was released on 9 September 2013 and was named album of the year by The Arts Desk. It also received a nomination at Gilles Peterson's awards. That same year the band won the MOBO Award for best jazz act. Lest We Forget What We Came Here to Do from 2015 received the same nomination. The third album, Your Queen Is a Reptile, came out on 30 March 2018 on Impulse! and was nominated for the Mercury Prize. The fourth, Black to the Future, followed on 14 May 2021 and was called an eloquent dance between rage and joy by The Observer. In June 2022 the band announced that it was closing this chapter for the time being.

The sound is danceable and urgent: a heavy tuba as the foundation, two drummers who complement each other and a saxophone that rises above it sharp and melodic. Sons of Kemet belonged to the new wave of British jazz, in which young musicians mixed their jazz with rock, Caribbean and African music and political messages. In this way the group brought jazz to a new, young audience.
artiest/sons-of-kemet.listen: Listen to My Queen Is Harriet Tubman and notice the tuba, which plays the role of the bass, and the driving rhythm of the two drummers. Follow how the saxophone above it becomes ever more urgent.

artiest/sophie.text:
SOPHIE, in full Sophie Xeon, was a British music producer, songwriter and DJ. She was born in Northampton and later grew up in London. Her father took her to raves from an early age and bought rave cassettes that they played in the car, on which she became hooked on electronic music. As a child she wanted to leave school to become a producer. She started in the band Motherland, played live in Berlin and the United Kingdom in 2008 and 2009 and then worked on remixes and short films. Her first single, Nothing More to Say, was released in 2013, followed by Bipp and Elle.

The singles from the early years, including Lemonade and Hard, were collected on Product in 2015. She worked with artists from the label PC Music, such as A. G. Cook and GFOTY, and produced for Charli XCX, Vince Staples, Kim Petras and Madonna. At first she kept her identity hidden; in 2017 she came out openly as transgender. In 2018 the album Oil of Every Pearl's Un-Insides was released, which received a Grammy nomination for best dance/electronic album. She died in January 2021 after a fall in Athens. Her second album, Sophie, was completed by her brother Benny Long and was released in 2024.

Her style combined experimental sound design, sugar-sweet synthesizer sounds and underground dance music. She is regarded as one of the pioneers of hyperpop and the bubblegum bass of the 2010s. Critics described her as someone who bridged the gap between mainstream and avant-garde as few others did.
artiest/sophie.listen: Listen to Immaterial and notice the sounds that do not sound like ordinary instruments, but like toys, bells and plastic. Notice how sweet the chorus is and how strange and danceable the rhythms beneath it are.

artiest/soulja-boy.text:
Soulja Boy, real name DeAndre Cortez Way, is an American rapper. He was born in Chicago in 1990, grew up in Atlanta and at fourteen moved with his father to Batesville in Mississippi. His father gave him a recording studio, and from 2005 he put his music on sites such as Newgrounds and SoundClick, later also on YouTube and Myspace. In this way he built an audience on the internet before a record label knew him.

In 2007 he released the single Crank That (Soulja Boy) himself, with a cheaply made video in which he showed the accompanying dance. The record led to a contract with Collipark Music, a label of Interscope Records, and spent seven weeks, not consecutively, at the top of the American Billboard Hot 100. The debut album Souljaboytellem.com was released in 2007 and was reportedly recorded with only the demo version of FL Studio. After that came iSouljaBoyTellem in 2008, with Kiss Me thru the Phone, and The DeAndre Way in 2010. His music is simple and danceable, with simple beats, short choruses and lyrics that revolve mainly around the dance and the party feeling. Critics were often negative and predicted that he would remain a one-hit wonder.

What matters most for pop history is how he worked. He used social media and digital marketing early and successfully to make himself known, something that later became normal for artists. After The DeAndre Way he continued independently and founded his own label, Stacks on Deck Entertainment, where Lil B and Riff Raff, among others, signed.
artiest/soulja-boy.listen: Listen to Crank That (Soulja Boy). Notice how little happens in the beat and how the instructions for the dance are worked into the lyrics themselves.

artiest/soulsonic-force.text:
Soulsonic Force, also known as Afrika Bambaataa & Soulsonic Force, is an American electro-funk and hip hop group. It was originally led by Afrika Bambaataa, who helped put hip hop on the map in the early 1980s. The group also played a role in the emergence of the electro movement in the United States.

In 1982 the single Planet Rock was released. The song borrowed musical motifs from German electro-pop, from British rock and from African American disco rap, and fused them into a single sound. In doing so it offered hip hop a new image of worldwide harmony. The record was an instant hit and charted around the world. Other well-known songs by the group are Looking for the Perfect Beat and Renegades of Funk, which is one of the first politically conscious rap songs, alongside The Message by Grandmaster Flash & the Furious Five. Later the group also sang on the title track of the Freestylers' debut album, We Rock Hard.

The group showed that hip hop could be more than rap over a funk loop: it pointed the way to modern dance styles such as electro-funk and Miami bass. In the course, Planet Rock is the listening tip for the chapter on electronic music, because of the melody that comes from Kraftwerk.
artiest/soulsonic-force.listen: Listen to Planet Rock and notice the melody. Can you hear the melody of Trans-Europe Express by Kraftwerk, now over a heavy hip hop rhythm with a drum machine?

artiest/soundgarden.text:
Soundgarden was an American rock band from Seattle, founded in 1984 by the singer and drummer Chris Cornell, the guitarist Kim Thayil and the bass player Hiro Yamamoto. The name came from an artwork in a park in Seattle: a sound sculpture of pipes through which the wind blows. Before long a permanent drummer took over the drums, so that Cornell could concentrate on singing; from 1986 that was Matt Cameron. Ben Shepherd became the permanent bass player in 1990. The band was the first of a series of grunge bands on the label Sub Pop, and in 1988 the first grunge band on a major label.

After the EPs Screaming Life (1987) and Fopp (1988) came the albums Ultramega OK (1988) and Louder Than Love (1989). The breakthrough came with Badmotorfinger (1991), with the singles Jesus Christ Pose, Outshined and Rusty Cage. MTV refused the video for Jesus Christ Pose, and many listeners found the song anti-Christian. Cornell explained that it was in fact a criticism of famous people who present themselves with the image of Jesus as a victim. Superunknown (1994), with Spoonman and Black Hole Sun, entered at number 1 in America. In 1997 the band split up, and in 2010 a reunion followed. Cornell died in 2017.

Soundgarden, with Nirvana, Pearl Jam and Alice in Chains, was one of the big names of grunge, but sounded heavier than most of its contemporaries. Critics heard the riffs of Black Sabbath and Led Zeppelin in it, mixed with the rawness of punk. Low-tuned, heavy guitar riffs and Cornell's wailing screams made the band recognisable.
artiest/soundgarden.listen: Listen to Jesus Christ Pose and notice the drums and the bass, which drive the song along like a machine, with Thayil's guitar screaming through it. Hear how Cornell screams out high above it all.

artiest/sousa-s-band.text:
Sousa's Band was the civilian concert band of the American composer and conductor John Philip Sousa, known as the March King of the United States. Sousa was born in 1854 in Washington, D.C. His father played trombone in the Marine Band and enrolled him as an apprentice at thirteen, to prevent him from joining a circus orchestra. There he learned violin, piano, flute and wind instruments, and turned out to have perfect pitch. In 1880 he became leader of the Marine Band and made it the country's most important military band, with more symphonic music and stricter rehearsals.

In 1892 Sousa left the army and founded his own group. It toured from 1892 to 1931 and gave 15,623 concerts, in the United States and beyond, including at the world exposition in Paris and at the Royal Albert Hall in London. In Paris the band marched through the streets to the Arc de Triomphe. In the early 1920s the saxophonist Jascha Gurewich played with it as a soloist. His marches include The Stars and Stripes Forever, Semper Fidelis, The Liberty Bell, The Thunderer and The Washington Post. He also helped in the development of the sousaphone, a marching tuba. During the First World War he led the navy band near Chicago. He died in 1932.

The band's music consists of clear, powerfully constructed marches, with trumpets, trombones and percussion setting the beat and a melody that is immediately singable. With his tours Sousa brought wind music to a wide audience, at a time when there was as yet no radio or recorded pop.
artiest/sousa-s-band.listen: Listen to The Washington Post and notice the tight beat of the drums and the clear trumpet melody. Hear how the piece is built in blocks and how each section brings a new sound.

artiest/southern-syncopated-orchestra.text:
The Southern Syncopated Orchestra was an early jazz group that brought Black musicians to the United Kingdom. The composer Will Marion Cook founded it, first in the United States as the New York Syncopated Orchestra. Its members included the clarinettist Sidney Bechet from New Orleans, the British singer Evelyn Dove, who performed under the name Norma Winchester, and the soprano Hattie King Reavis. Between 1919 and 1921 the orchestra toured Great Britain and Ireland.

The programme was broad. The orchestra played classical music, ragtime, blues, spirituals and jazz, and made successful annual tours of Great Britain and the Continent. It was very popular: in 1920, 328,000 people bought a ticket for performances at Kelvin Hall in Glasgow. On the farewell tour of 1921 it played for three weeks at the Lyric Theatre in Glasgow, in October, the company's last performances.

On the way to Dublin the ship SS Rowan sank in thick fog off the coast of Wigtownshire, after being struck by two other ships. Of the 120 people on board, 36 died, among them nine musicians. All the instruments were lost. Theatres in Glasgow organised benefit concerts for the survivors. On 17 October 1921 the orchestra nevertheless performed in Dublin, then in Derry and Belfast, and in November it ceased to exist. In 2013 two of the musicians who died, the singer Frank Bates and the drummer Pete Robinson, were commemorated with blue plaques in London.
artiest/southern-syncopated-orchestra.listen: Listen to an early recording of Sidney Bechet from the 1920s. Notice his broad, trembling clarinet or soprano saxophone sound, which leaps out of the orchestra.

artiest/spandau-ballet.text:
Spandau Ballet was an English pop band from Islington in London, formed in 1979. The group grew out of the post-punk and dance culture of the capital and began under the name The Applause as house band of the Blitz Kids' club night, where it played European dance music. The classic line-up consisted of Gary Kemp on guitar, synthesizer and backing vocals, his brother Martin Kemp on bass, the singer Tony Hadley, the saxophonist Steve Norman and the drummer John Keeble. Gary Kemp wrote the songs.

The first single, To Cut a Long Story Short, reached fifth place in the United Kingdom in 1980 and was the first of ten British top-ten hits. The album Journeys to Glory was released in 1981, followed by Diamond in 1982 and True in 1983. The title track True became a number 1 in the United Kingdom and also reached the American top five. Parade, Through the Barricades and Heart Like a Sky followed. In 1990 the group gave its last concert before a break of nineteen years. In 2009 it returned with a tour, and in 2017 Hadley left the band.

Spandau Ballet belonged to the New Romantic wave, and became one of its most successful groups. Its music combines dance rhythms and synthesizers with smooth, romantic vocals. In the course it appears alongside ABC and Culture Club in the description of the 1980s.
artiest/spandau-ballet.listen: Listen to True and notice the soft guitar, the saxophone and the full singing voice of Tony Hadley. How does this ballad sound compared with the dance pop of the band's early days?

artiest/spice-girls.text:
The Spice Girls are a British girl group, put together in London in 1994. The management company Heart Management placed an advertisement in the trade paper The Stage and held auditions for a girl group that was to compete with the British boy bands. After a change, there were five singers: Geri Halliwell, Melanie Brown, Emma Bunton, Melanie Chisholm and Victoria Adams, later Beckham. With more than 100 million records sold, they are regarded as the best-selling girl group ever.

In 1995 the five broke away from their creators, chose Simon Fuller as manager and signed with Virgin. In July 1996 Wannabe was released in England, written by the group with the producers Matt Rowe and Richard Stannard. According to Mel B the song was finished in half an hour. Wannabe is a pop song with a rapped passage just before the last chorus and the invented word 'zigazig-ah' at the end of the chorus. It spent seven weeks at number 1 in England, also became number 1 in the Netherlands and in 1997 spent four weeks at number 1 in the United States. The debut album Spice (1996) sold more than 23 million copies worldwide. In 1997 came the album Spiceworld and the film Spice World.

The group had a slogan, girl power, and a nickname for each member: Ginger, Scary, Baby, Sporty and Posh. In this way the band became a brand with dolls, soft drinks and clothing. In May 1998 Halliwell left. Reunions followed later, including at the closing ceremony of the London Olympic Games in 2012.
artiest/spice-girls.listen: In Wannabe, notice how each member gets a line or voice of her own, so that you hear the five characters before you see them. Listen also to the rapped middle section and the invented word 'zigazig-ah', which lingers like a hook at the end of the chorus.

artiest/spider-murphy-gang.text:
The Spider Murphy Gang is a German rock band from Munich. In 1977 the banker Günther Sigl founded the group, together with Barny Murphy, Michael Busse and the drummer Franz Trojan. The name comes from the fictional gangster Spider Murphy in the song Jailhouse Rock by Elvis Presley. The aim was to play old rock 'n' roll songs. Through the radio presenter Georg Kostya the group got airtime and became known in the region.

In 1980 the first album, Rock 'n' Roll Schuah, was released, with songs in the Bavarian dialect and down-to-earth themes. A year later, in the autumn of 1981, the band became known throughout West Germany with Skandal im Sperrbezirk, a song of the Neue Deutsche Welle. In the spring of 1982 it also became a hit in the Netherlands and Flanders. Later singles were Schickeria and Wo bist Du. In 1982 a film about the band appeared, and in 1983 it was the first West German group to perform in the GDR.

The musical emphasis lies on classic rock 'n' roll, with guitar playing inspired by Chuck Berry. A recurring element in the lyrics is the humorous but also critical view of the sex industry. Skandal im Sperrbezirk is about the red-light district of Munich. In the course the group represents the 1980s in Germany, with rock 'n' roll in the native language.
artiest/spider-murphy-gang.listen: Listen to Skandal im Sperrbezirk and notice the rock 'n' roll rhythm and the guitar that recalls Chuck Berry. Can you also hear the dialect in the singing?

artiest/spinderella.text:
Spinderella, real name Deidra Muriel Roper, is an American DJ, rapper and producer. She was born in 1970 and grew up in Brooklyn in New York, one of five children. As a child she was fascinated by her father's record collection. At fourteen she began as a DJ, learning the techniques from a local DJ she hung out with. At sixteen a classmate asked whether she would be interested in a girl group in hip hop.

That is how she came to producer Hurby Azor in 1986, just before a performance by the group at the Westchester Music Festival. The group's original DJ, Latoya Hanson, had been missing rehearsals and performances. Azor chose Roper as her replacement and gave her the name Spinderella, around the time the first album came out. With Salt and Pepa she formed a trio that became one of the most successful female hip hop acts ever. The group made five studio albums and had several gold and platinum singles. Spinderella also produced a number of songs on those albums. Salt-N-Pepa's records showed that hip hop could come from women too, with the DJ as a fixture behind the turntables.

Outside the group she rapped on Big Daddy Kane's Very Special in 1993 and played small parts in films. From 2003 to 2006 she presented the programme The BackSpin on radio in Los Angeles, featuring old-school hip hop. Later she founded the Spinderella DJ Academy. In 2019 she announced that Salt-N-Pepa had fired her. In 2025 she was inducted with the group into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, as the first female DJ.
artiest/spinderella.listen: Listen to Push It by Salt-N-Pepa. Notice the scratches and the rhythm of the record, and try to hear what the DJ adds to it alongside the vocals of Salt and Pepa.

artiest/spontaneous-music-ensemble.text:
The Spontaneous Music Ensemble, SME for short, was a loose association of freely improvising musicians, brought together in 1965 by the South London jazz drummer and trumpeter John Stevens and the alto and soprano saxophonist Trevor Watts. The line-up varied from a duo of Stevens and Watts to a company of more than a dozen players. In January 1966 the group began a residency of six nights a week at the Little Theatre Club in London. The month after, it recorded its first album, Challenge.

The principle was open and leaderless. According to the critic Brian Olewnick, great value was placed on careful listening. The saxophonist Evan Parker related that Stevens had two rules: if you play so loudly that you can no longer hear the others, it is too loud, and if your music does not regularly relate to what the others are doing, why are you in the group? Out of this came what was jokingly called insect improv: very quiet, intense, rhythmless and mostly atonal music. The early groups centred on wind instruments, with Watts, Parker and the trumpeter Kenny Wheeler, the later ones on strings, with the guitarist Roger Smith and the violinist Nigel Coombes. The transitional album is Biosystem from 1977. Derek Bailey, Paul Rutherford, Dave Holland and Barry Guy also played with the group.

The group drew inspiration from American free jazz and from AMM, and from Anton Webern and Samuel Beckett. The final line-up was a trio of Stevens, Smith and the saxophonist John Butcher. Stevens died in 1994, which meant the end of SME. The ensemble showed that improvisation can above all be a matter of listening.
artiest/spontaneous-music-ensemble.listen: Listen to Questions & Answers and notice how the players answer each other almost without words. Notice how quiet and focused the music is and how some sounds come only after a silence.

artiest/st-germain.text:
St Germain is the artist name of the French musician and DJ Ludovic Navarre, born in 1969 in Saint-Germain-en-Laye near Paris. He began releasing music in 1991 and was one of the first French artists to sign with the label of Laurent Garnier and Eric Morand. Under all kinds of names he made techno and deep house. From 1993 he used St Germain for his deep house. As influences he named, among others, Bob Marley, Toots & The Maytals, Miles Davis and Kool and the Gang.

In 1995 the album Boulevard was released, which the British magazine Mixmag chose as album of the year. That success brought him to Blue Note, the jazz label from 1939. There he made Tourist, which came out in 2000, with songs such as Rose Rouge, Sure Thing and So Flute. The album appeared just as lounge music was on the rise, and brought St Germain to a large audience. After that it went quiet for a long time. Only in 2015 was the album St Germain released, recorded with African musicians, with the kora, the balafon and the ngoni from Mali alongside electric guitars, piano and saxophone.

St Germain's music blends house with jazz: a continuous dance beat and electronic loops, with real instruments such as horns, piano and flute over the top, and samples from old blues and jazz recordings. In this way he belongs to the nu jazz that emerged around 1990 in London and Paris, in which DJs and producers brought jazz back to the dance floor. That a jazz label such as Blue Note signed him shows how close those worlds had come.
artiest/st-germain.listen: Listen to So Flute and notice how the song is built: a calm house beat that keeps going, with the flute of the title and other acoustic instruments over it. Can you hear where the electronics stop and the jazz begins?

artiest/staatsorchester-stuttgart.text:
The Staatsorchester Stuttgart, in full the Württembergisches Staatsorchester, is a German symphony orchestra from Stuttgart. It is based at the Staatstheater Stuttgart, where it plays for productions of the Staatsoper and for the Stuttgart Ballet. In addition it regularly gives concerts in the Beethovensaal of the Liederhalle. Its roots lie in the Württembergische Hofkapelle, the court orchestra of the duchy. In 2018 the orchestra celebrated its four hundred and fiftieth anniversary.

In the twentieth century well-known conductors stood at its head. Fritz Busch led the orchestra from 1918 to 1922, Ferdinand Leitner from 1947 to 1969 and Dennis Russell Davies from 1980 to 1987. Later music directors included Lothar Zagrosek, Manfred Honeck and Sylvain Cambreling. Since 2018 Cornelius Meister has been Generalmusikdirektor. In 2002 the magazine Opernwelt chose the ensemble as orchestra of the year.

The recordings show how broad the repertoire is, from opera to ballet and concert music. The list includes Wagner's Ring des Nibelungen, Schönberg's Moses und Aron, Hindemith's Symphonic Metamorphosis, and newer works such as Akhnaten by Philip Glass and Tabula Rasa. It is a typical opera orchestra of a German city, which lives mostly below stage level in the theatre and carries the music of the performances there.
artiest/staatsorchester-stuttgart.listen: Listen to an excerpt from this orchestra's Ring project, for example Das Rheingold. Notice how the orchestra builds the atmosphere without singers, with low strings and brass carrying the action.

artiest/stan-getz.text: Tenor saxophonist Stan Getz grew up in the Bronx and as a teenager already played in big bands. He took the light, soft tone of Lester Young as his model. In 1947 he joined the saxophone section of Woody Herman, the 'Four Brothers'; with his ballad solo in Early Autumn (1948) he became known. His sound was called 'The Sound'. In 1961 he recorded Focus, with strings by Eddie Sauter. A year later followed Jazz Samba with the guitarist Charlie Byrd, with which bossa nova broke through in America. Getz/Gilberto, with João and Astrud Gilberto and Antônio Carlos Jobim, became one of the best-selling jazz albums. Getz struggled with addiction, but kept playing until his death.
artiest/stan-getz.listen: Listen to the tone: soft, smooth and yet clear.

artiest/stan-getz-en-joao-gilberto.text:
Stan Getz, an American saxophonist, and João Gilberto, a Brazilian singer and guitarist, made the album Getz/Gilberto together, which was released on Verve Records in March 1964. The pianist and composer Antônio Carlos Jobim played on it and wrote many of the songs. The album was recorded in March 1963 in New York, under producer Creed Taylor, with Phil Ramone as engineer. On two songs, The Girl from Ipanema and Corcovado, Astrud Gilberto sings, who had never sung professionally before.

Bossa nova had come into being in 1958, through Gilberto and Jobim, among others. Getz had become enthusiastic in the early 1960s and had already had success in 1962 with Jazz Samba and Big Band Bossa Nova. After a bossa nova concert at Carnegie Hall in 1962, Taylor wanted to bring the two Brazilians together with Getz. In the studio the differences sometimes ran high: Gilberto liked a delicate approach and found Getz too loud, and their language barrier was bridged by Jobim. The album received Grammys for best jazz album and best engineering, and The Girl from Ipanema received the Grammy for record of the year. In 1965 it was the first non-American album to be named album of the year. More than a million copies were sold.

The music is restrained and calm. Gilberto sings almost in a whisper, the guitar plays the rhythm and Jobim keeps his piano minimal. Above it Getz plays his soft, warm tenor saxophone. The record made bossa nova known worldwide and showed that jazz and Brazilian music could form a natural blend.
artiest/stan-getz-en-joao-gilberto.listen: Listen to The Girl from Ipanema and notice João's soft, almost whispered voice, followed by Astrud's, and the calm guitar beneath. Can you hear how Getz then gently takes over the melody with his saxophone?

artiest/stan-kenton.text:
Stan Kenton was an American pianist, composer, arranger and bandleader. He was born in 1911 in Wichita, Kansas, and grew up in California. At sixteen he was already playing regular gigs as a pianist. In the 1930s he worked in clubs and with orchestras, including Gus Arnheim's. In 1940 he founded his first orchestra, with which he played at the Rendezvous Ballroom in Balboa, California, in 1941. From 1943 he recorded for the new label Capitol Records. Eager Beaver became a well-known record. The singer June Christy and the arranger Pete Rugolo were part of the core of the band from 1945.

Kenton's orchestra sounded different from the swing bands of his time. With plenty of brass, rhythms from Latin America and influences from modern classical composers such as Stravinsky and Bartók, Rugolo helped build a heavy, powerful sound, which made the Artistry in Rhythm band famous. In 1947 the period of Progressive Jazz began, with work by Rugolo and Bob Graettinger. Graettinger's City of Glass premiered in 1948 and was recorded in 1950 for the Innovations Orchestra. According to the source, critics wrote about that music sometimes scathingly, and sometimes with respect. Kenton kept looking ahead, even when he had hits.

Kenton was also a pioneer of jazz education. In 1959 he started the Stan Kenton Jazz Camp at Indiana University. He led an innovative jazz orchestra for almost forty years and also kept making albums such as Kenton in Hi-Fi, Kenton's West Side Story and Adventures in Jazz. He died in 1979. For anyone who wants to understand the big band and West Coast jazz, he is an important link.
artiest/stan-kenton.listen: Listen to Artistry in Rhythm or Eager Beaver. Notice the heavy block of brass and how the band plays with force, rather than with light swing.

artiest/standards-trio.text:
The Standards Trio is the name of the trio of the pianist Keith Jarrett with the bass player Gary Peacock and the drummer Jack DeJohnette. It began in 1983. Manfred Eicher, the head of the label ECM, suggested to Jarrett that he record an album of jazz standards. Jarrett asked Peacock and DeJohnette for it, with whom he had worked in 1977 on Peacock's album Tales of Another. The result was called Standards, Vol. 1. Standards, Vol. 2 and Changes came from the same recording session and followed shortly after.

The albums and the tour that followed were successful, at a time when traditional acoustic post-bop was on the rise again. The trio continued for years alongside Jarrett's solo concerts. Around 2000, when Jarrett began touring again after an illness, he played both solo and with the Standards Trio.

The music consists of well-known songs from the American song tradition, as they are used in jazz, in an acoustic line-up of piano, bass and drums. The trio plays the songs without much frill and lets them breathe. Jarrett, who had earlier played with Art Blakey, Charles Lloyd and Miles Davis, brought his art of improvisation to the repertoire of the standards in this trio. In this way the group joined the jazz tradition to the sound quality of the ECM recordings. Jarrett is known for his album The Köln Concert from 1975, but the Standards Trio showed another side of him: the interpreter of the songbook.
artiest/standards-trio.listen: Listen to a standard from Standards, Vol. 1. Notice how piano, bass and drums follow one another, and how Jarrett lets go of the familiar melody and picks it up again.

artiest/stanley-clarke.text: Bass player Stanley Clarke from Philadelphia played both double bass and bass guitar. He played young with Horace Silver, Joe Henderson and Pharoah Sanders, and in 1972 became a member of Chick Corea's Return to Forever. There he made the bass guitar a solo instrument, with slap technique and fast lines. His solo album School Days (1976) became a model for bass players from jazz, rock and funk. Later he worked a great deal in Hollywood as a film composer. With Corea and Lenny White he reunited Return to Forever in 2008.
artiest/stanley-clarke.listen: Hear how the bass is out in front and plays the melody.
